# 0. Raw data quality check
Samples were sequenced across two separate runs (two run-specific folders). This script matches corresponding files between the two run folders (based on a run-specific ID pattern) and concatenates them into a single FASTQ file per sample.
```
DIR1="run1"          # First sequencing run folder
DIR2="run2"          # Second sequencing run folder
OUTPUT_DIR="combined_data"

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

# Detect the run-specific ID pattern in each folder
# (based on the first file found in each folder)
PATTERN1=$(ls "$DIR1" | head -n 1 | grep -oE "A[0-9A-Z]{7}")
PATTERN2=$(ls "$DIR2" | head -n 1 | grep -oE "A[0-9A-Z]{7}")

# Check that both patterns were successfully detected 
if [[ -z "$PATTERN1" || -z "$PATTERN2" ]]; then
    echo "Could not detect the distinct run ID patterns"
    exit 1
fi

# Loop over files in the first run folder 
for file1 in "$DIR1"/*.fastq.gz; do
    # File name without the path
    filename=$(basename "$file1")

    # Build the corresponding file name in the second run folder
    file2="$DIR2/${filename/$PATTERN1/$PATTERN2}"

    # Check that the matching file exists in the second run folder
    if [[ -f "$file2" ]]; then
        # New file name, replacing the run ID pattern with "combined"
        new_filename="${filename//$PATTERN1/combined}"
        new_filename="${new_filename//$PATTERN2/combined}"

        # Concatenate the two files
        cat "$file1" "$file2" > "$OUTPUT_DIR/$new_filename"
        echo "Combined files: $file1 + $file2 -> $OUTPUT_DIR/$new_filename"
    else
        echo "No matching file found for $file1"
    fi
done
```

Runs FastQC on the raw FASTQ files (before trimming).
```
LOCAL_FASTQ_DIR="raw_data"
FASTQC_OUTPUT_DIR="results_fastqc_raw"

module load FastQC/0.12.1
mkdir -p "$FASTQC_OUTPUT_DIR"
fastqc -t 4 -o "$FASTQC_OUTPUT_DIR" "$LOCAL_FASTQ_DIR"/*.fastq.gz
```

Aggregates the per-sample FastQC reports (from the raw reads, step 01) into a single MultiQC report.
```
FASTQC_RESULTS="results_fastqc_raw"
OUTPUT_DIR="results_multiqc_raw"

module load multiqc/1.9
multiqc "$FASTQC_RESULTS" -o "$OUTPUT_DIR"
```

# 1. Trimming
Runs fastp on each paired-end sample (R1/R2), producing cleaned FASTQ files plus per-sample HTML/JSON QC reports.
```
RAW_DIR="raw_data"
OUTPUT_DIR="results_trimming_fastp"
ADAPTER_FASTA="adapters.fa"

module load fastp/0.20.1

# Build the list of R1 files and select this array task's sample
R1_FILES=($(ls ${RAW_DIR}/*_R1.fastq.gz | sort))
R1=${R1_FILES}
R2=${R1/_R1.fastq.gz/_R2.fastq.gz}

# Sample name for output files
SAMPLE=$(basename ${R1} | sed 's/_R1.fastq.gz//')

# Run fastp
fastp \
  -i "${R1}" \
  -I "${R2}" \
  -o "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${SAMPLE}_clean_R1.fastq.gz" \
  -O "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${SAMPLE}_clean_R2.fastq.gz" \
  --disable_adapter_trimming \
  --adapter_fasta "${ADAPTER_FASTA}" \
  --html "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${SAMPLE}_fastp.html" \
  --json "${OUTPUT_DIR}/${SAMPLE}_fastp.json" \
  -w "${SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK}"
```

# 2. Build the HISAT2 genome index
Builds the HISAT2 index from the reference genome FASTA file, used downstream for read alignment. 
```
GENOME_DIR="reference_genome"
GENOME_FASTA="${GENOME_DIR}/reference_genome.fasta"
INDEX_PREFIX="${GENOME_DIR}/genome_index"

module load hisat2/2.2.1
hisat2-build "${GENOME_FASTA}" "${INDEX_PREFIX}"
```

# 3. Read alignment with HISAT2
Aligns each trimmed paired-end sample to the reference genome index (built in step 04), and outputs a coordinate-sorted BAM file per sample. Runs as a SLURM array job, one task per sample.
```
FASTQ_DIR="results_trimming_fastp"
INDEX_DIR="reference_genome"
INDEX="${INDEX_DIR}/genome_index/genome_index"
OUTPUT_DIR="hisat2_mapped"

module load hisat2/2.2.1
module load samtools/1.19.2

mkdir -p "${OUTPUT_DIR}"

# Build the list of R1 files and select this array task's sample
R1_FILES=($(ls ${FASTQ_DIR}/*_R1_trimmed.fastq.gz | sort))
R1=${R1_FILES}
R2=${R1/_R1_trimmed.fastq.gz/_R2_trimmed.fastq.gz}

# Sample name for the output file
SAMPLE=$(basename ${R1} | sed 's/_R1_trimmed.fastq.gz//')
OUT="${OUTPUT_DIR}/${SAMPLE}.sorted.bam"

echo "Starting mapping for ${SAMPLE}..."
echo "Input files: ${R1} and ${R2}"

# Alignment, then convert to a coordinate-sorted BAM
hisat2 -x ${INDEX} \
    -1 ${R1} \
    -2 ${R2} | \
samtools view -bS - | \
samtools sort -o ${OUT}

echo "Mapping done for ${SAMPLE}. Output file: ${OUT}"
```

# 4. Gene-level read quantification with featureCounts
Counts paired-end fragments per gene from the sorted/marked BAM files, using the reference GTF annotation, producing a single merged count matrix across all samples.
```
ANNOTATION_GTF="reference_genome/annotation.gtf"
BAM_DIR="picardTool_results/ddFilesMark"
OUTPUT_DIR="featureCounts_results"

module load singularity/4.0.1
module load subread/2.0.6

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

# Run featureCounts in paired-end + fragment counting mode
featureCounts \
  -T 4 \
  -p \
  --countReadPairs \
  -t exon \
  -g gene_id \
  -a "$ANNOTATION_GTF" \
  -o "$OUTPUT_DIR/featureCounts_all_samples.txt" \
  "$BAM_DIR"/*.bam
```
